title.narrative: Supporting Innovation in Water and Sanitation in Egypt

description.narrative: In recent years Egypt has been suffering from water scarcity and is considered a water poor country with a current yearly shortage of 23 billion cubic meters. Climate change will further exacerbate the situation and pose significant challenges to the water sector as it is expected to cause significant variation in the flow of the Nile water. Additionally, other factors pose significant challenges such as: 1) the pollution of the Nile river with municipal and industrial waste and the leakage of wastewater 2) The inefficient use of water in households and in irrigation system 3) The water leakage from the infrastructure network due to the lack of maintenance 4) the uneven distribution of water; in addition to increasing water demand caused by an increase in the population (expected to grow by 60 to 75% by 2050). The situation is worse in rural areas than it is in urban areas. Particularly, the vulnerable Upper Egyptian rural communities suffer from lack of water for long times and must spend long hours searching for alternative water sources, which is both time consuming and financially expensive. Most of those communities resort to household water pumps to get ground water, and often this water is highly contaminated due to the mixing with sewage water. These communities are the most prone to be affected with these risks of potable water scarcity and quality. Additionally, sanitation services present a significant challenge. While most of the villages are connected to the water system, many are not connected to a sanitation system, which forces residents to build informal sewer systems or on-site sanitation systems. In addition, excess sludge is often thrown into nearby water bodies. The situation in even worse in areas with higher ground water levels which are often contaminated especially in dense urbanized areas. In Nile delta for example, the situation continues to worsen due the rising water tables and consequently, groundwater and water drains and canals are polluted and contaminated, posing one of the biggest challenges to public health. Accordingly, this project has two main objectives. Firstly, it aims at providing access to affordable, clean and safe potable water and sanitation services through using cost-efficient and innovative approaches to vulnerable rural residents in Upper Egypt and in the Nile Delta (Damietta tbc); secondly, it aims at ensuring the sustainability of water and sanitation service provision through research activities, building capacities and scaling up and institutionalizing the models provided. Approach: This project is based on the human rights, local empowerment and knowledge strengthening approaches, aiming to reduce the vulnerability of defined groups and to enhance the resilience of the overall sector. This will be achieved through enabling clean water provision and supporting improved sanitation services, improving capacities of local administration to respond to water needs, and creating a strong knowledge foundation with the necessary partnerships to institutionalize developed provision models for the long-term sustainability of water and sanitation provision. Main Expected Accomlishments: • Improved access to clean water and sanitation for more than 70,000 vulnerable rural inhabitants in selected sites in three locations in Upper Egypt and one in Nile Delta. • Improved capacity of local staff to ensure efficient management, maintenance and quality control of constructed units. • Strengthened advocacy and partnership on knowledge creation and institutionalization of innovative and efficient service provision models
